name: Wisconsin
redemption: None post-sale (2-year delinquency before county takes deed)
keyNotes: Rural Wisconsin strong for land and recreational property
Environmental title risks in industrial counties — always check DNR records before bidding on former industrial land
summary: Wisconsin counties sell tax deeds after 2-year tax certificate. Milwaukee and Dane have best inventory. Online infrastructure is growing but limited. Some counties use land banks. Statute: WS §74.57.
typeWhy: Wisconsin sells the property deed outright after a 2-year tax certificate period during which the county holds the delinquent property. There is no post-sale redemption. WS §74.57.
rateWhy: Wisconsin is a deed state with no statutory interest rate. Returns are market-driven at auction. WS §74.57.
notBeginnerReason: 2-year redemption, limited centralized platform, and county-by-county coordination required.
beginnerTip: Milwaukee and Dane (Madison) counties have the best WI inventory. Contact the Milwaukee County Treasurer specifically — they have the most organized auction process in the state.
risks: Some counties use land banks rather than public auctions
ddExtra: Contact the county treasurer to confirm the 2-year delinquency threshold has passed
Check the Milwaukee County Land Records System for upcoming actions
Verify whether the county plans to auction vs. use a land bank for specific parcels

auctionSignup.platform: County treasurer (varies — Milwaukee uses online system)
steps: Find your target county treasurer at wi.gov/government/counties
Contact the treasurer to confirm the delinquency threshold and upcoming sale schedule
Milwaukee County has online auction capabilities — check milwaukee.county.gov/treasurer

otc.note: Check county land bank for properties not in public auction.

tylerCompliance.summary: Status pending — monitoring for legislative action.
tylerCompliance.details: This state compliance with Tyler v. Hennepin County (2023) is currently being monitored. Aurigen tracks legislative updates, pending bills, and court decisions that affect tax sale surplus requirements. Check back for updates.

featuredCounties.name: Milwaukee
featuredCounties.notes: Best inventory in WI. Online capable.

rules.critical: ⚡ Wisconsin does NOT sell tax lien certificates to private investors (§74.57(3) prohibits county from selling, assigning, or transferring tax certificates). County holds all certificates.

process.step1: Taxes delinquent after Jan 31. Interest + penalty: 1%/month from Feb 1. Washington County confirmed: 1.5%/month = 18%/yr.
process.step2: September 1: County treasurer issues Tax Certificate for ALL parcels with unpaid taxes as of Aug 31. Includes all delinquent real property taxes, special assessments, special charges, special taxes.
process.step3: Treasurer mails notice to homeowner within 90 days of certificate issuance (§74.59).
process.step4: 2-year redemption period begins. Owner may redeem by paying all delinquent amounts + interest + penalties + costs.
process.step5: After 2 years without redemption — county may pursue ONE of 3 title-taking paths.

titlePaths.path1_taxDeed: Tax Deed Process (§75.12, §75.14): County applies to county clerk for tax deed. Clerk issues deed to county. County records deed.
titlePaths.path2_mortgage: Mortgage Foreclosure Process (§75.19): County forecloses using same process as mortgage lender. Court-supervised.
titlePaths.path3_inRem: In Rem Statutory Foreclosure (§75.521): County files petition with court listing all delinquent properties. Most common in rural/smaller counties. Court enters judgment. GAL appointed for minors/incompetents.

auction.frequency: After county takes title — county sells at public auction. As scheduled by county.
auction.platform: County-run — in-person or online depending on county
auction.note: County must sell property after taking title per §75.35. Timing varies by county.

otc.name: County-Owned Tax-Deeded Properties
otc.process: Contact county treasurer or clerk directly. Counties may offer unsold tax-deeded properties.
otc.note: No standard OTC lien cert sales — county holds all certs

subTax.name: N/A — No private lien cert holders in Wisconsin

delinquencyInterest.milwaukee: ⚡ Milwaukee County: 18%/yr (1.5%/month) — confirmed per county treasurer

redemption.period: 2 years from issuance of tax certificate (September 1 of certificate year)
redemption.delayException: If treasurer fails to mail required notice — redemption period starts from mailing date, not certificate date
redemption.erosionException: 1-year redemption if county incurred expenses for erosion control
redemption.amounts: All delinquent taxes + special assessments + special charges + interest + penalties + costs

deedPath.name: Tax Deed to County / Foreclosure Judgment (3 paths)
deedPath.titleEffect: County takes title. Then sells to new owner.
deedPath.restrictionsSurvive: ⚡ Covenants and restrictions running with land SURVIVE tax deed (§75.14(4)) — unlike most states
deedPath.challenge: Former owner may challenge within limitation period set by §75.27. Notice required before limitation runs.

surplus.name: Excess Sale Proceeds
surplus.statute: Wis. Stat. §75.35 (sale of county-held property) + Tyler v. Hennepin (2023)
surplus.process: Post-Tyler: Wisconsin counties must return surplus to former owner. State law changed after Tyler ruling.
surplus.note: ⚡ Pre-Tyler: WI counties kept surplus. Now excess must go to former property owner after county recoups taxes + costs + interest.

es.summary: Los condados de Wisconsin venden escrituras fiscales después del certificado fiscal de 2 años. Milwaukee y Dane tienen el mejor inventario. La infraestructura en línea está creciendo pero es limitada. Algunos condados usan bancos de tierras. Estatuto: WS §74.57.
es.typeWhy: Wisconsin es un estado de escritura porque los condados venden escrituras fiscales después de un período de certificado de 2 años, sin derecho de redención posterior a la venta (WS §74.57).
es.rateWhy: No se aplica tasa de interés ya que es un estado de escritura. Algunos condados usan bancos de tierras en lugar de subastas públicas (WS §74.57).
es.notBeginnerReason: Redención de 2 años, plataforma centralizada limitada y se requiere coordinación condado por condado.
es.beginnerTip: Milwaukee y Dane (Madison) tienen el mejor inventario de WI. Contacte específicamente al Tesorero del Condado Milwaukee — tienen el proceso de subasta más organizado del estado.
risks: Ciclo de 2 años antes de la subasta
Algunos condados usan bancos de tierras en lugar de subastas públicas
ddExtra: Contacte al tesorero del condado para confirmar que el umbral de morosidad de 2 años ha pasado
Revise el Sistema de Registros de Tierras del Condado Milwaukee para próximas acciones
Verifique si el condado planea subastar vs. usar un banco de tierras para parcelas específicas

auctionSignup.platform: Tesorero del condado (varía — Milwaukee usa sistema en línea)
steps: Encuentre al tesorero de su condado en wi.gov/government/counties
Contacte al tesorero para confirmar el umbral de morosidad y el próximo calendario de venta
El Condado Milwaukee tiene capacidades de subasta en línea — revise milwaukee.county.gov/treasurer

otc.note: Revise el banco de tierras del condado para propiedades no en subasta pública.
